title: [Project] I translated the full PHP 8.4.26 HTTP-only RCE research repository into English, including technical documentation and code comments
description: This research project documents a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in PHP version 8.4.26 under the official production configuration. The exploit chain uses only HTTP requests and includes an ASLR bypass via out-of-bounds memory disclosure. It does not require enabling display_errors or modifying the default 128 MB memory limit. The attack involves multi-stage exploitation including PHP session-state corruption, heap manipulation, and control-flow hijacking. The exploit was successfully reproduced on an Apache prefork configuration with a 10/10 success rate in the tested environment. The repository provides detailed technical documentation, code comments, and evidence of the exploit's effectiveness. The translation effort makes the original Chinese research accessible to the international security community.

aiSummary: The project translates and documents a complex HTTP-only remote code execution exploit against PHP 8.4.26. The exploit chain bypasses ASLR by leveraging out-of-bounds memory reads and uses PHP session-state corruption and heap manipulation to hijack control flow, ultimately achieving code execution without requiring display_errors to be enabled or memory limits to be changed. The exploit works on the official PHP production configuration and Apache prefork MPM with MaxRequestWorkers=150. It involves pinning workers, chunked multipart requests to bypass post_max_size, and precise memory layout manipulations. The research includes extensive technical notes, failed attempts, memory layout analysis, and reproducible proof-of-concept code. The translation effort aims to make this detailed research accessible to English-speaking security professionals.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation results in remote code execution on servers running PHP 8.4.26 with default production settings, including display_errors=Off and memory_limit=128M. This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary system commands remotely via crafted HTTP requests without requiring any configuration changes or enabling debugging features. The exploit has been demonstrated with a 10/10 success rate in tested environments, indicating high reliability under the specified conditions.
